sources.dates: Signed Vienna, 18 April 1961; entered into force 24 April 1964

sources.scope: Establishment of diplomatic relations and functions of missions; accreditation and credentials; classes of heads of mission and precedence (Arts. 13-18); inviolability of mission premises, archives and correspondence; diplomatic privileges and immunities; tax and customs exemptions.

sources.dates: Done at Vienna, 24 April 1963; entered into force 19 March 1967
sources.publisher: United Nations — International Law Commission; UN Treaty Series, vol. 596, p. 261
sources.scope: Establishment of consular relations; consular functions (Art. 5); classes of heads of consular posts; appointment and admission (exequatur); consular privileges and immunities; Art. 36 (communication with nationals); honorary consular officers.

sources.dates: Signed San Francisco, 26 June 1945; entered into force 24 October 1945
sources.scope: Purposes and principles of the UN (Arts. 1-2: sovereign equality, maintenance of peace and security); membership; principal organs; framework underlying the Vienna Conventions.

sources.name_en: Published FCDO Protocol Directorate protocol guide
sources.note: The existence of the Protocol Directorate was confirmed from an official GOV.UK page opened directly (FCDO privacy notice for foreign diplomatic and consular staff, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fcdo-privacy-notice-foreign-diplomatic-staff-in-the-uk/fcdo-privacy-notice-foreign-diplomatic-and-consular-staff-in-the-uk), which states the Diplomatic Missions and International Organisations / Ceremonial Unit is responsible for protocol and ceremonial matters. No published protocol guide (PDF or guidance page) from FCDO was found. A 2013 FCDO blog post on protocol is an opinion piece by a former official, not an official published guide, and is not relied on.
sources.publisher: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) — Protocol Directorate
sources.scope: Would cover UK protocol practice for diplomatic missions in London, if a published guide existed.

sources.name_en: Official Arabic text of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations 1961 on a UN site
sources.note: The official English text is verified (VCDR-1961-EN). The ILC page on legal.un.org offers language options including Arabic, but no working direct Arabic URL was extracted in this review. Complete Arabic texts exist on non-official sites (e.g. aajeg.com, lawsociety.ly, a university PDF) and are NOT listed here as official sources. Arabic is not one of the five authentic languages of the Convention (Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish).
sources.scope: Arabic version of the VCDR, if an official UN Arabic text were located.
